title: Safepath experiments: gated model releases and A/B comparisons behind version pins
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need a gated experimentation workflow for publishing new model versions that are pinned per customer or route, enabling safe A/B tests and shadow runs without disrupting pinned traffic. The goal is a 'safepath' mechanism that lets PMs/Engineers configure small, measurable experiments for a new model version behind an existing version pin, collect latency/cost/quality signals, and either ramp, roll back, or promote the version. This ticket covers the product requirements and acceptance criteria for the PM surface and runbook; engineering tickets will capture runtime, routing, and metrics plumbing.
acceptance_criteria: Console: Ability to create a Pin-Gated Experiment that targets a pinned route/model and specifies buckets (e.g., 0.5%, 5%, shadow) and evaluation metrics.
API: New rollout object in REST API that accepts 'pin_target', 'variant_versions', 'buckets', 'evaluation_profile', and 'auto_rollback_policy'.

Metrics: Experiment emits per-variant telemetry: token-latency, p95, cost_per_request, failure_rate, and a quality_score derived from configured evals; performance profiles published for the new version must be linked to the experiment UI.
Safety: Default auto-rollback triggers on >30% regression in quality_score or >2x latency increase at p95 versus baseline, with immediate re-routing to the pinned version.
Permissions: Only users with rollout:create permission can start experiments; audit log entry is created for each rollout action.
Observability: Dedicated experiment dashboard with trend lines, cohort breakdown, per-customer impact, and link to evaluation prompt set results.
Documentation: Quickstart doc and runbook for interpreting signals and performing manual rollbacks or promotions.
E2E: An internal end-to-end experiment can be started, observed, and either promoted or rolled back in staging using a synthetic prompt set.
implementation_notes: Introduce a Rollout API object and expand the 'pin' model to accept gated-experiment hooks. Backend routing service must be able to split traffic by percentage for pinned routes (not just global routes).

Runtime: Leverage existing smart-routing layer to route by policy; add evaluation hooks that sample outputs for quality evals without violating customer privacy—use internal synthetic datasets unless customer opt-in.

Performance profiles: When a new model version is onboarded, publish a performance profile (latency distribution, memory, throughput) to the model catalog; the console should surface these profiles next to experiment configuration.
Telemetry: Add experiment_id tag to requests and responses; emit aggregated metrics to metrics pipeline and to experiment dashboard. Ensure cost estimation per bucket is computed and displayed.
Rollbacks: Implement an automatic rollback executor that evaluates policy thresholds and can revert routing decisions within 30s of detection.
RBAC & Audit: Integrate with SSO and Console permissions; write rollout events to audit log store for compliance.
Data retention: Experiment traces should follow platform retention rules; raw user outputs should not be stored for experiments unless explicitly allowed by customer contract.
testing_plan: Unit tests for Rollout API validation and permission checks.
Integration tests that create experiments against a staging runtime with two model versions and assert correct splitting, telemetry emission, and rollback behavior.
Load testing to validate that low-percentage buckets do not degrade global routing performance and that autoscaling recommendations account for experiment traffic.
Quality regression harness: run the configured evaluation prompt set against baseline and candidate versions and ensure quality_score calculation is stable.
Security review to verify no customer data leak when using shadow/eval modes; privacy tests to confirm only synthetic traces are retained by default.
timeline: Week 1: PM finalizes UX flows and acceptance criteria; align on rollback thresholds and default settings.
Week 2-3: Engineering implements Rollout API and basic routing support; model profile publishing hook landed.
Week 4: Instrumentation and experiment dashboard; QA runs integration and load tests.
Week 5: Staging experiment with internal tenants; iterate on thresholds and UX.
Week 6: Documentation, runbook, and gradual roll-out to select customers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Experiment traffic could accidentally bias global autoscaling and increase cost. Mitigation: Tag experiment traffic separately and exclude from certain autoscaling heuristics until proven stable.
Risk: Quality signals noisy for small buckets. Mitigation: Require minimum sample size or extended observation windows for auto-promote decisions.
Risk: Privacy/regulatory concerns when sampling real customer requests. Mitigation: Default to synthetic evals and opt-in for customer data sampling; require legal review for PII-containing datasets.
Risk: Complex rollbacks causing oscillation. Mitigation: Implement cooldown windows and require manual confirmation for repeated rollbacks.
